title: Train the 84-field model with the linear masking rate
headline: Two trainings that differ only in the masking rate, read before any battle
setup: The model fills a team of six Pokémon, 84 fields in all, where each field is one value such as a species or a move. In training some fields are hidden, and the masking rate is the chance that a field is hidden. This ticket trains two models on the shuffled-only table and reads their validation loss before any battle.
alt: The two trainings differ only in the masking rate. Before any battle, each model's validation loss is read under both masking rates. A t check on the per-field model then decides whether Per-field, corrected t is battled: it is battled only at 0.01 or more.
terms: The chance a field is hidden in training. Per-field, ours: species are almost never hidden. Linear, the papers': every field has the same chance
The loss on teams held out of training. Lower is better. It is only comparable under one masking rate
The training teams whose win-rate labels come only from battles that shuffle a team's six Pokémon
The t at which training hid as many fields as are still hidden at this pass
Measures how far the model's choices move when told the corrected t: 0 is no change. Under 0.01, the correction cannot matter, and the row is not battled
The row that samples the per-field model while telling it the corrected t

right.title: Linear model

frames.takes: Only the masking rate differs, so a gap between the two models can be pinned on it.
frames.measured: Both use the same 214,598 teams, one seed each, and at most 80 epochs.

frames.title: 2. Validation loss over training
frames.takes: Each line tracks one model's validation loss as its training runs.
frames.expected: Both curves fall and flatten, and neither turns upward.
frames.surprise: One curve turns upward, a sign of overfitting, and its run stops early.

frames.title: 3. Each model under each masking rate
frames.takes: Each model should score best under the masking rate it trained on.
frames.expected: The linear model is lower under the linear rate and slightly higher under the per-field rate.
frames.surprise: The linear model is lower under both rates.

frames.title: 4. The t check on the new per-field model
frames.takes: The t check measures how far the model's choices move when told the corrected t.
frames.expected: Every field type stays under 0.01, as on today's default model, and the row is not battled.
frames.surprise: One field type reaches 0.01, and Per-field, corrected t is battled.
